intro.text: deploy.local, agent-first. Scout keeps the dev loop moving; Warden watches apps and computers. Light work runs free on SER (Qwen3-8B on Lemonade); code and review use Claude and Codex. Every screen loads the deploy.local design system (Theme menu).

desktop.text: Desktop app: Electron on Mac, Linux and Windows; iOS stays SwiftUI. The window loads deploy.local from your coordinator, trusting only its CA. The shell adds the menu bar or tray, notifications, a login item, the bundled worker (installing the app adds a computer) and the native control helper for screen use. It notifies only for Waiting on you items and failing apps.

cli.text: CLI proposal. Today bin/deploy.js is one 3,389-line file with 36 command lines and 25 global options. Proposed: six groups in the app's words, [app] as an optional positional, steps instead of log dumps, the dark theme's palette, --json everywhere and exit code 3 while something waits on you. Old commands keep working for one release.

build.text: Build rules for v2: the server sends each conversation as typed events (decision, work log, task link, answer, report) and every client renders them, folding but never dropping a decision. Tabs appear only once their thing exists. Words are taught once, where they first happen. Agents brief once a day and otherwise speak only when needed.

mac-chrome-how.text:
Proposal. Electron titleBarStyle hiddenInset: the traffic lights live in the first 92 px of the 52 px top row.

• Expanded: the 256 px sidebar shows only the d mark beside the lights, then Search and Collapse. Each control keeps a 32 px target; the brand name remains accessible. Full screen restores the wordmark and removes the light gutter.
• Collapsed: one 64 px rail, also at 700 px. Its items start below the 52 px top row. The lights extend into reserved space beside it; the main header starts 44 px inside the main pane (108 px from the window edge). No mark or title sits under the lights.
• One device preference across Projects, a task’s Changes, a project’s Code and Design. New devices start expanded. Page changes and resizing never change that preference. The expanded sidebar stays 256 px at 700; secondary content folds instead.
• Drag empty top-row space; buttons, links and fields remain clickable. Double-click follows the Mac zoom setting. Design panels fold independently and never hide the app sidebar.
• These boards show both saved choices. Native lights and their reserved space exist only in the Mac app.

welcome-narrow-note.text: For approval. In the browser, below 820px the welcome sidebar hides and the menu button opens it. In the Mac app, follow the Mac chrome boards instead: the saved expanded sidebar or rail stays on the left at 700px, with a dedicated top-row reserve for the traffic lights.

design-canvas-how.text:
How it works. Designs live in the repo, so any agent (Codex, Claude) or a person can change them on a branch:
• design/canvas.json: sections, board positions, notes
• design/boards/<Name>.html: one self-contained board, styled by the shipped design-system CSS
• design/notes/<Name>.md: what the board is for and the decisions behind it
A visual change is a design change on a branch. Its task gets a Design tab with Before (main) and After (this branch). Approving merges design/ into main, which makes the After the design; then the build task starts. deploy.local renders all of it; no claude.ai needed.

design-canvas-changes.text:
Design: how it works
• Designs live in the repo in design/: canvas.json plus one HTML file per board, built from the design system. Every element has a stable layer ID (data-layer).
• Layout follows Figma: navigation on the left (the d menu with Waiting on you, Designs and the branch, File | Assets, Pages = sections, Layers), the full properties panel on the right, the tool bar at the bottom with vector tools.
• Edits save to a design branch; main changes only through Propose for review and approval (Design tab, chat card, Waiting on you).
• Agents edit through design tools (read, render, structured edits, presence, comments, propose), each on its own branch, shown as a live overlay you accept or discard.
• iPad uses the desktop layout; iPhone has the full canvas with Layers and Edit as sheets.

Build order:
1. Canvas, Layers, Comments, review, and Ask an agent with live editing.
2. Direct edits: text, properties and tokens.
3. Vector tools and Assets.

design-review-notes-how.text:
Reviewing changes that are not boards
• Opening a design item in Waiting on you shows its review, task or not: changed boards as Before and After, and changed canvas notes as their text, Before and After, with the new lines marked.
• The list on the left names each change: a board by its name, a note by its first line, tagged Note.
• The item's line says what changed in words: “The note “Drawing: how it works” changed on design/drawing-note”, or “2 boards and 1 note changed”; never “1 design files”.
• iPhone shows the same: the note's text in place of a board, with Before and After.

design-prototype-how.text:
Prototype and Play: how boards connect
• Links already live in the boards: a layer that opens another board carries its link (href). 143 of 171 boards have them.
• Prototype, beside Edit and Comments, draws the selected board's links on the canvas: a line from each layer to the board it opens, the selected layer's line strongest. The repeated sidebar links stay hidden until you show them.
• To see every connection while you move around the canvas, in any tab, turn on Connections in the tool bar (⇧C); see the Connections board.
• With a layer selected, Interaction says what a click does: On click › Go to a board. Change the board, remove the link, or drag the dot at the layer's edge onto a board. Saving writes the layer's link on your design branch, like any edit.
• The board section lists where the board leads and what leads to it; Flow says where Play starts (the page's first board unless you choose another).
• Play (▷, top right) opens the start board full screen and follows links: Back, the trail of boards you passed through, Restart, and the width (1440, 700, 390). Clicking where there's no link lights up the links. Esc or Exit returns to the canvas.
• On iPad, Play is tap to follow, swipe from the left edge to go back, Done to leave.

design-draw-how.text:
Drawing: how it works
• Rectangle, Ellipse and Line (the shape menu, or R, O, L) draw inside a board where you drag. The shape keeps that spot (X and Y) and size, filled surface with a line stroke, and saves to the board on your design branch.
• Text (T): click inside a board to place a text layer and type; Enter keeps it.
• Pen (P): a stroke with Apple Pencil, or a drag, inks a mark on the canvas: danger, W 2.5, the same width on screen at any zoom. Marks sit beside boards like sticky notes, never inside one, and save to canvas.json. Select one to set its rotation, size, opacity, stroke colour, W and Arrow end; drag it to move it; Delete removes it. Tapping points instead draws a vector in a board; Enter, or a tap on the first point, ends it.
• Frame (F): drag on empty canvas to make a new board (Web 1440 or Phone 390 by its width, named Board N until you rename it); inside a board it makes a frame layer.
• Sticky notes (S): click on the canvas; they save to canvas.json and show over the boards they point at. Layers lists a page's marks and sticky notes after its boards.
• Escape goes back to Move (V); the pen keeps inking until you do. Layers drawn in a board can be edited in the properties panel and undone with Reset.

design-native-how.text:
Design on iPhone and iPad
• Projects › a project › Design opens the Design page full screen, signed in as you. ‹ goes back to the project.
• iPad shows the desktop layout (the iPad board) and draws with Apple Pencil through the pen tool; iPhone shows the phone layout (these boards).
• Approving from Waiting on you and the design card in a task's chat stay native and show rendered boards.
• Ask has no agent choice: a design ask runs as its own task, on any free computer or the one you pick.

projects-rail-how.text:
One sidebar choice, remembered everywhere on this device
• New devices start with the full 256 px sidebar. Collapse selects the 64 px rail on Projects, Changes, Code and Design alike. There are no page-kind defaults or separate memories.
• Collapse sits beside Search; Expand sits above the account in the rail. ⌘\ toggles the same preference everywhere. Page changes and resizing preserve it; both states fit at 700 px.
• The rail keeps New task, Projects, Live, Computers, Design, Waiting on you and Settings on the left. Hover or keyboard focus names each icon. Agents and Today remain in the full sidebar, one Expand or ⌘K away.
• MacChromeNarrow shows this same rail with a 52 px top strip for native lights and a clear header. Full screen removes that strip and its gutter.
• DesignMac and DesignConnections show an owner who chose the rail. Hiding Design panels affects only those panels, never the app navigation.

design-connections-how.text:
Connections: see how boards link without opening Prototype
• Connections, the last button in the tool bar (⇧C, also in the zoom menu), draws every link between boards on the page as an arrow, in Edit, Prototype and Comments alike. It stays on until you turn it off, per person.
• Arrows run board to board, one per pair, however many layers make that link. They're grey and thin so the boards stay readable.
• Select a board and its arrows turn violet: the boards it leads to and the boards that lead to it. Selecting a layer lights only that layer's link.
• Links to boards on other pages don't draw; the board's Connections section lists them under their page. Clicking a row goes to that board.
• Repeated links, like the sidebar on every board, stay hidden; the eye on the Sidebar row draws them too.
• Narrow windows show the same arrows; the Connections section sits in the bottom sheet.

self-update.text: SER is released like any other app, by pushing to its repository. Its update status and recovery pages remain under Computers → deploy.local updates. There is no SER update entry in the sidebar, for administrators or anyone else. The former sidebar status layers now live within those pages. Preparing and activating a SER release still verifies the build, backs up the databases and restores the previous release if health checks fail. Mac app updates are separate and appear only inside the Mac app.

mac-app-update.text:
deploy.local for Mac updates
• Check GET /desktop/version on the coordinator this Mac app is connected to, on launch and every 4 hours. Use its version and short commit, and the darwin-arm64 target’s file, size and sha256. The commit and byte counts on these boards are example data.
• Only the Mac app shows the update row, immediately above the account. It never appears in a browser and never describes SER updating itself. No row when the app is current; a failed background check must not claim it is current.
• Update available starts downloading the published /desktop/ zip. Progress uses actual bytes and total size; Cancel stops and discards the partial download, leaving the installed app unchanged. Downloading 42% rounds 54 of 130 MB.
• After download, show Checking download… in the same row. Check SHA-256 against the published value before anything changes; only then offer Restart to update. A mismatch leaves the old app untouched and offers Try again. Network errors use “The download stopped. Nothing was changed.” with Try again.
• Restart to update is one press: remember the current page, show Installing… briefly, quit, replace the app in place and reopen on the same coordinator and page. Keep the old app until the new one opens successfully; restore it if installation or launch fails. Do not silently discard the previous app.
• The collapsed rail shows an update glyph above the account with a named tooltip. Pressing it expands the shared sidebar so the owner can read the status and choose Download or Restart; it does not start either action by itself. The chosen expanded state is remembered everywhere.
• The install handoff and restoring the same page require implementation verification after this design is approved; these are static review boards.
